headline_marked: [[White House forces Anthropic to pull AI models offline]] amid real-time rule-making
headline: White House forces Anthropic to pull AI models offline amid real-time rule-making
summary: The White House issued an export control directive to Anthropic, forcing its advanced AI models offline over alleged ties to China. This highlights a 'Wild West' era of AI regulation.
details: The Trump administration issued an export control directive to Anthropic, one of the world's leading AI labs. This forced the company to pull its most advanced models, Claude Mythos and Fable 5, offline, sparking days of negotiations with the White House.

Anthropic maintains it did not violate any concrete procedures or rules, according to a source close to the company. However, the White House contends that Anthropic acted recklessly, demonstrating a lack of trustworthiness in rolling out frontier technology safely.

This ongoing dispute highlights what many are calling the 'Wild West' era of American AI regulation. With few explicit laws governing frontier AI development, companies face trouble for crossing unspoken lines.

A former White House technology official criticized the administration's 'slap-dash approach,' arguing there should have been systematic policies in place. President Trump has previously blocked efforts to impose AI guardrails, reversing Biden-era frameworks and creating a task force against state laws.

Despite public reporting, the dispute remains opaque, with the US government not clearly stating Anthropic's specific wrongdoing. The best public explanation came from a general post on X by White House technology adviser David Sacks.

Ironically, the White House's directive has hampered innovation by demanding Anthropic prohibit foreign nationals from accessing Mythos and Fable 5. This prevents many of Anthropic's own employees and major customers like Apple and Meta from using its cutting-edge models.

The White House's concerns reportedly stemmed from Anthropic sharing Mythos with SK Telecom, a South Korean firm allegedly tied to China. Additionally, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy raised concerns about circumvention of guardrails on Claude Fable 5.

Anthropic claims it coordinated with the US government on Mythos's rollout and immediately revoked access when concerns were raised. Regarding Fable 5, the company and researchers argue that jailbreaking is an inherent, complex issue with probabilistic AI models, not easily 'solved'.

headline_marked: [[Meta's AI Unit in Meltdown]] Amid Employee Revolt; Thiel's Secret Group Leaked
headline: Meta's AI Unit in Meltdown Amid Employee Revolt; Thiel's Secret Group Leaked
summary: Internal dysfunction plagues Meta's new AI unit, with employees calling it 'the Gulag' and openly rebelling. Meanwhile, details of Peter Thiel's secretive 'Dialog' group have leaked, and Sam Bankman-Fried is reportedly seeking a pardon from the Trump administr
details: Meta's new AI unit, Meta Superintelligence Labs, is facing severe internal dysfunction and low morale. Employees transferred to the applied AI engineering unit have reportedly called it 'the Gulag' due to widespread dissatisfaction.

During a recent employee-only meeting for the applied AI unit, an individual interrupted the call to state they were 'being the company's bitch' and urged others to tell a Meta AI executive he was 'a piece of shit.' This incident highlights the extreme frustration within the team.

Leaked online messages have revealed details about 'Dialog,' an invite-only group co-founded by billionaire Peter Thiel. Over 200 high-profile individuals from government, tech, and academia are listed as members and guests, discussing various topics behind closed doors.

Convicted felon and former cryptocurrency founder Sam Bankman-Fried is actively seeking a pardon from the Trump administration. He is also reportedly planning a potential comeback, adding to a busy week for controversial figures in tech.
